12.title: IDP solutions that already work in communities must be scaled up nationwide!
12.excerpt: During a working trip to Volyn, Minister for Communities, Territories and Internally Displaced Persons of Ukraine Vitalii Bezghin visited a dormitory of Lutsk National Technical University, which is now home to 113 internally displaced persons.

blocks.p: During a working trip to Volyn together with Members of Parliament Viacheslav Rublov and Serhii Kozyr, Minister for Communities, Territories and Internally Displaced Persons of Ukraine Vitalii Bezghin visited a dormitory of Lutsk National Technical University. Today it is home to 113 internally displaced persons — students and teachers from the eastern regions of Ukraine. The university has created decent living conditions: modern living quarters, kitchens, a shelter and a barrier-free environment.

Olena Fomina, Professor at the Department of Marketing, came from Donetsk and has been working at the university for a year now. This is the key point — full integration: having a home, studying, working, using services and gradually becoming part of the local community.

The Minister thanked the university management and the regional and city authorities for their productive joint work and proactive approach. It is exactly this kind of effective approach that should become national practice.

blocks.quote: “Our task is to involve the Ministry of Education and Science, the Ministry of Social Policy, regional military administrations, international partners, local self-government and educational institutions in order to develop a clear roadmap for scaling up this approach. We must ensure that successful projects do not remain isolated examples but become a systematic policy for the development of Ukraine’s regions — above all in the western oblasts, which today host a large number of internally displaced people,” Vitalii Bezghin stressed.

13.title: Timely evacuation is a decision that saves lives
13.excerpt: The heroes of the information campaign on timely evacuation are people who have gone through this journey themselves and moved to safer regions of the country to save their lives.

blocks.p: The heroes of the information campaign on timely evacuation are people who have gone through this journey themselves.

Maryna and Mykhailo’s family, Alla Bronislavivna and Andrii Ivanovych, Liudmyla Antonivna, Ivan Hryhorovych and Valentyna Oleksiivna moved to safer regions of the country to save their lives. In upcoming posts we will tell how they made this decision and how they settled in their new homes.
We are grateful to them for sharing their stories!

Everything you need to know about evacuation is available from the 1548 hotline. Find out about payments, housing and free transport, including for people with limited mobility and families with children.

23.title: Housing vouchers for IDPs from the temporarily occupied territories: the first families have already bought new homes
23.excerpt: Under the eRecovery state programme, Ukrainians are already actively using housing vouchers worth UAH 2 million to buy new homes. 160 families have already completed their purchases.

blocks.p: Under the “Housing for IDPs from the Temporarily Occupied Territories” component of the eRecovery state programme, Ukrainians are already actively using housing vouchers to buy new homes. The programme provides housing vouchers worth UAH 2 million to internally displaced persons from the temporarily occupied territories who have the status of combat participant or person with a disability caused by the war.

blocks.quote: “The programme is already delivering real results for people: 160 families who lost their homes because of the war and were forced to leave the temporarily occupied territories have already completed their transactions and bought new homes. And these are only the first weeks of the mechanism. We see that people are actively using the vouchers all over the country — from Kyiv Oblast to Zakarpattia — and choose for themselves where to build a new life. At the same time, more than 860 transactions have already been submitted for payment, so hundreds more families will receive their own homes in the near future. We are working to attract additional funding and expand the programme so that as many Ukrainians as possible can buy their own home,” said Oleksii Kuleba, Deputy Prime Minister for Restoration of Ukraine — Minister for Development of Communities and Territories of Ukraine.

blocks.p: Most homes have been purchased in Kyiv Oblast, where 61 vouchers worth more than UAH 121 million have already been used.
The leaders also include:

ul: Dnipropetrovsk Oblast — 29 vouchers worth UAH 58 million;
Mykolaiv Oblast — 20 vouchers worth UAH 40 million;
Kyiv City — 16 vouchers worth UAH 32 million;
Odesa Oblast — 9 vouchers worth almost UAH 18 million.

blocks.p: The programme covers a number of regions. In total, housing vouchers have already been used in 14 oblasts of Ukraine, including Khmelnytskyi, Vinnytsia, Ivano-Frankivsk, Chernivtsi, Poltava, Ternopil, Lviv, Zakarpattia, Kirovohrad and Volyn.

More than 91% of the purchased properties are apartments, and about 8% are private houses. Almost 87% of the homes were bought on the secondary market. The housing voucher mechanism works actively on the real estate market and allows families to choose housing according to their own needs.
In total, more than 39,000 applications have been submitted to the programme. More than 30,000 of them have already been reviewed and approved by local commissions.
At the first funding stage, 3,296 applications for booking housing vouchers with a total value of UAH 6.59 billion were approved under the programme.

As a reminder, under the programme rules, if booked funds are not used within 60 days, they are returned to the programme and allocated to the next applicants. In this case, a person can apply again and rejoin the queue.

Work is also under way to attract additional funding from the state budget and international partners. In particular, the programme will be partly financed by a loan from the Council of Europe Development Bank of about EUR 80 million (≈ UAH 3.9 billion).

34.title: Planning is a key element of recovery, says Oleksii Riabykin
34.excerpt: At the presentation of the third phase of the “U-LEAD with Europe” programme, Deputy Minister for Development of Communities and Territories Oleksii Riabykin discussed the challenges and prospects of recovery of Ukrainian regions.

blocks.p: On 18 March, the third phase of the “U-LEAD with Europe” programme was presented in Kyiv. As part of the event, Deputy Minister for Development of Communities and Territories Oleksii Riabykin took part in the panel discussion “Local Recovery and Development: Ways Forward”. Together with Oleksandr Slobozhan, Executive Director of the Association of Ukrainian Cities, and Yurii Fomichev, Mayor of Slavutych, he discussed the challenges and prospects of recovery of Ukrainian regions.

Oleksii Riabykin emphasised that Ukraine’s recovery is taking place amid the challenges of war, which require clear coordination and a strategic vision. It is important that this process is not only fast but also systematic and focused on long-term development.

blocks.quote: “Ukraine is the only country carrying out recovery during a large-scale war. At the same time, we cannot act chaotically. Planning is a key element of recovery. That is why it is important to understand in advance what we are doing, when we are doing it and how much funding it requires. We are now in the process of strategic planning: updating state regional development strategies and helping communities approve their own strategies,” the Deputy Minister noted.

blocks.p: The participants also discussed recovery financing in 2025. Oleksii Riabykin noted that the third stage of the Ukraine Recovery Programme, for which projects are currently being selected, provides EUR 100 million for community initiatives. Another EUR 150 million is expected to be allocated to the next stage of the programme. In addition, a further EUR 200 million may be directed to social projects.

blocks.quote: “There is the issue of the frozen assets of the aggressor state — we are working to make them a source of recovery financing. At the same time, it is important to have a clear understanding of the budget in order to be transparent both for international partners and for citizens. When we talk about prioritisation, planning and public investment management reform, we must remember that this applies not only to the national level but also to the local level,” Oleksii Riabykin stressed.

blocks.p: The Ministry for Development is working on the procedure for using the funds of the State Regional Development Fund, restored in 2020. This concerns more than UAH 30 billion to support regional projects. The public investment management reform is also under way, which will allow funds to be distributed more efficiently and will contribute to the faster recovery of affected regions.
